title: Current fluctuations in a gas of active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particles
authors: Sandeep Jangid, Aman Kumbhakar, Juliane U. Klamser, Tridib Sadhu
abstract: We investigate the statistics of the time-integrated current in an infinite one-dimensional gas of independent active Ornstein--Uhlenbeck particles, as a model system for studying an active generalisation of the corresponding passive (diffusive) phenomenology. Unlike the latter, where current fluctuations exhibit universal sub-diffusive scaling, active systems display diffusive, super-diffusive, and sub-diffusive regimes over different time scales. We fully characterise the distribution of current in terms of large-deviation asymptotics, showing that all of these scaling regimes are described by a single scaled cumulant generating function. Moreover, the statistics retain a dependence on the initial condition even at large times, revealing a persistent memory of the initial state. We further obtain the joint large-deviation statistics of currents measured at two distinct times, characterising temporal correlations. Our analytical predictions are verified using rare-event importance sampling, which resolves probabilities as small as $10^{-1000}$.
summary: This work analyzes the current fluctuations in a model of active particles (AOUPs) using advanced statistical tools like large-deviation theory. It establishes that active systems exhibit complex, time-dependent scaling regimes unlike passive ones. The methodology involves calculating complex CGFs for both single-time and two-time current measurements, providing a detailed statistical characterization of non-equilibrium transport.
main_problem: The paper investigates the statistics of the time-integrated current in a gas of active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particles, contrasting its behavior with passive diffusive systems.
main_result: Active systems exhibit distinct diffusive, super-diffusive, and sub-diffusive scaling regimes for current fluctuations, and the statistics retain a memory of the initial state even at large times.
method: The analysis relies heavily on large-deviation theory, calculating Cumulant Generating Functions (CGFs) for both one-time and two-time current measurements.
model_or_system: The model is an infinite one-dimensional gas of independent active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particles (AOUPs), whose dynamics are governed by coupled equations for position and velocity.
key_observables: Time-integrated current ($Q_t$), joint probability distribution $P(Q_{t_1}, Q_{t_2})$, and the associated Large-Deviation Function (LDF) $\Phi(q)$.
important_parameters: Initial densities ($ho_a, ho_b$), time scales ($	au$), and the ratio of active to diffusive effects (related to $Pe^2/2D	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between 'annealed' and 'quenched' averaging procedures over initial conditions, and uses rare-event importance sampling for numerical verification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling of current fluctuation variances ($	ilde{\sigma}_t^2$ vs. time) showing multiple dynamical regimes, and show the joint probability distribution $P(Q_{t_1}, Q_{t_2})$ for different initial conditions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the CGFs for the current in various ensembles (annealed/quenched for position and velocity), analyzes the resulting scaling regimes, and extends the formalism to calculate the two-time joint current statistics.
why_interesting: The study of active matter dynamics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics is highly relevant to AMO physics, particularly in systems involving particle transport or driven quantum systems where non-Markovian effects and non-equilibrium fluctuations are key.
